name: Robert J. Shiller (Yale) — U.S. Stock Markets 1871–Present and CAPE Ratio
description: Robert Shiller's online data page: the monthly U.S. stock market dataset behind Irrational Exuberance and the CAPE ratio, plus annual long-term series and the home-price series from the book. The monthly stock dataset is this site's confirmed P/E history through Shiller's last confirmed month.

notes: One workbook; the Data sheet has several header rows above the monthly table. Parsed by scripts/fetch_sp500_pe.py (needs pandas and xlrd).

Confirmed 2026-09-15: the Yale copy (http://www.econ.yale.edu/~shiller/data/ie_data.xls) is frozen — downloaded file's OLE metadata reads Last Saved 2023-09-17, and its last monthly row with a price is 2023.09 (price 4515.77) with earnings only through 2023.06 (181.17). shillerdata.com is the maintained copy: the visible "download" button's target is not the page's obvious link text but an img1.wsimg.com CDN asset URL, findable in the page's raw HTML (a plain curl fetch suffices — no JS execution needed) via its `data-aid="DOWNLOAD_DOCUMENT_LINK_RENDERED"` anchor, with a `?ver=<timestamp>` cache-busting query param that may change; it resolves to a workbook last saved 2026-09-02 whose last row with a price is 2026.09 (price 7631.47) and with earnings through 2026.06 (295.3881) — i.e. current. scripts/fetch_sp500_pe.py still points at the Yale URL as of this check; repointing it is a code change out of this catalogue entry's scope.

The query-string version tag on the shillerdata.com URL was observed as ver=1788371540009 on 2026-09-15; if a future fetch gets a 404, re-derive the current link from https://shillerdata.com/ (Compilation of Cape Ratio -> ie_data.xls download link in the page's HTML).

terms.summary: Free download; no published terms on the Yale data page or shillerdata.com. Asked by email, Shiller's index advisor answered on 2026-09-17 that Shiller does not license the CAPE ratio, does not own its S&P components, and that S&P's wishes govern — so the S&P-derived columns (price, dividends, earnings, CAPE) follow S&P Dow Jones Indices' terms

datasets.name: U.S. stock markets 1871–present and CAPE, monthly
datasets.gives: Monthly S&P Composite price, dividends and earnings, the consumer price index, the long-term (10-year Treasury) interest rate, real (CPI-adjusted) price, dividends and earnings, and the cyclically adjusted price-earnings ratio (CAPE) with a total-return CAPE variant; all from January 1871
datasets.units: index points, dollars per share, percent, ratio
notes: Used by series/sp500_pe.json as confirmed history; months after Shiller's last confirmed month come from FRED SP500 and data/earnings_overrides.json.
Shiller periodically restates historical earnings; the site shows the latest revision (series/sp500_pe.json revision_note).

Refresh cadence is not stated on either page; irregular updates confirmed directly (see access.notes): the shillerdata.com copy carries monthly price through 2026-09 and monthly earnings through 2026-06, so the lag is unknown rather than guessed.

scripts/fetch_sp500_pe.py fetches from the Yale URL as of 2026-09-15, which is frozen at 2023-09 (price) / 2023-06 (earnings) — repointing it to the shillerdata.com URL above would restore live monthly updates; recorded here, not made, per this task's scope.

Also used by series/gs10_long.json (S11a, 2026-09-17) for its "Rate GS10" column, 1871-01 through 1953-03 only, stitched to FRED's GS10 from 1953-04. Neither this workbook nor Shiller's data pages document where the pre-1953 figures come from — checked 2026-09-17 (data.htm, online.htm, data/peratio.html, data/chapt26.xlsx, the Data/Disclaimer sheets); the two legs agree almost exactly at the seam (both 2.83 for 1953-03/1953-04), and finance-literature searches attribute the pre-1953 figures to Sidney Homer's A History of Interest Rates, but no Shiller-authored page states it — see catalog/research-log.md (2026-09-17). Unlike price/dividends/earnings/CAPE, this column has no S&P component, so it is not swept into the restricted treatment below; the site owner decided 2026-09-17 to publish it (see this file's notes and catalog/CLAUDE.md).

2026-09-17: Laurence Black (signing as Index Advisor to Robert J. Shiller) answered by email, verbatim: "Prof Shiller does not formally license usage of the ratio as we do not own the underlying components and thus ownership of the CAPE ratio is not assured. You will certainly have to adhere to S&P's wishes. We don't control who uses the ratio." It is neither a grant nor a refusal: Shiller's side claims no rights it could license and points to S&P. terms.status stays unknown because there is still no published terms page to cite (the quote is from private email, so it lives here rather than in terms.quote, which is for a sentence from a terms page); in practice every ie_data.xls column built from S&P price, dividends or earnings inherits spglobal's restricted terms, and the four sp500_* series stay presentation.publish false. The reply speaks only of the CAPE ratio; it does not address the long-term interest rate column (chart 4), which has no S&P component; the site owner decided 2026-09-17 to treat the pre-1953 long-rate data as free to use, so chart 4 publishes.
